Frequently asked questions

Source: vignettes/articles/faq.Rmd
faq.Rmd

pool() gives an error about mira objects, or does the wrong thing

mice also exports pool(). Whichever package is attached last masks the other, so library(mice) after library(missingmed) makes pool() mean mice::pool(). Call mice::mice() with the prefix instead of attaching mice, or call missingmed::pool(). The missingmed version forwards anything that is not a missingmed fit (a mice::mira, for example) to mice::pool(), so it is safe to keep missingmed’s pool() in front.

Monte Carlo interval or MBCO test?

They answer different questions. infer(type = "mc") gives a confidence interval for the indirect effect from the pooled estimates. infer(type = "mbco") gives a likelihood-ratio test of H0:ab=0H_0: ab = 0 and needs the per-imputation fits, so call it on the result of run(), not of pool(). vignette("mbco-mi") covers the test; vignette("worked-analysis") uses both.

Why does infer() ask for treatment_level?

The outcome model has a treatment-by-mediator interaction, so the indirect effect is a(b+θ3x)a (b + \theta_3 x) and depends on the treatment level xx. missingmed does not pick xx for you. For a 0/1 treatment, 1 gives the total and 0 the pure natural indirect effect. Section 3A of vignette("technical") has the details.

What does ariv do?

It applies to infer(type = "mbco") and mbco_d4(). With ariv = "fixed" (the default), every imputation’s likelihood ratio is taken on the branch the stacked constrained fit chose (a=0a = 0 or b=0b = 0). With ariv = "own", each imputation uses its own winning branch, which reproduces missingmed 0.4.0. The branch diagnostics are properties of the returned MbcoMIResult.

How many imputations do I need?

The pooled variance adds (1+1/m)B(1 + 1/m)B to the within-imputation variance, and the Monte Carlo error of everything computed across imputations shrinks as mm grows. A practical check: rerun with a larger m and a different seed, and see whether the conclusions move. The fmi column of pool(fit)@tidy_table reports the fraction of missing information per coefficient.

My model has a moderator. Can I use it?

Not in set_md_mediation(), which allows only main effects of the treatment and mediator plus one X:M term (see the Supported models article). mbco_d4() tests the indirect effect of a moderated model on a list of completed datasets.

Binary mediator or outcome?

Set family_m = binomial() or family_y = binomial(). The indirect effect is then a product of coefficients on the link scale, not a difference in probabilities; section 5A of vignette("technical") explains the caveat.

MI or IPW?

method = "mi" takes a mids object and pools across imputations. method = "ipw" takes the raw data frame and reweights the complete cases by the inverse probability of being complete, with sandwich standard errors by default. MBCO is not available for IPW fits.

What scale is delta in sensitivity_mnar() on?

The scale of the target variable’s imputation model: an additive shift for a continuous target, a log-odds shift for a binary one. Section 5B.2 of vignette("technical") shows how to translate a delta into a statement about non-respondents.

Why does infer() warn that an argument was ignored?

Some arguments apply to one inference type only, such as level, n.mc and treatment_level for "mc" and ariv for "mbco". Passing one to the other type warns, so a typo or a mismatched argument is not silently dropped.

Structural equation models and latent mediators?

The S7 pipeline fits regression models through medfit. Latent mediators are available only through the deprecated S4 API for now; a lavaan engine for set_md_mediation() is planned for 0.6.0. See the Migrating from the S4 API article.

How do I cite missingmed? 

citation("missingmed")
